admission.notes: Software structure is parsed from source artifacts by deterministic, stated rules. Every connection in this profile is extracted from an artifact, never declared as an opinion.

methods.change_coupling: change coupling (Zimmermann et al. 2005): per file pair, support = transactions containing both files; confidence = support / transactions containing either file; pairs below the stated minimum support are not reported
methods.hotspot: hotspot (Tornhill 2015): per file, changes = the number of transactions (commits, merge commits excluded) in the stated window that touched the file; complexity = the sum of the cyclomatic complexities of the file's functions and methods, absent unless every one was measured; the reported score is changes x complexity, with both factors always shown

id_grammar.package_rule: A node's package is the first :: segment of its id; external:: stubs are nobody's package.

location.ordering: file, then 1-based line, then optional 1-based column

measured_fields.extraction_rule: The last source line of the declaration, 1-based and inclusive (CODE_SCHEMA section 3). Core-reserved field: it keeps its 1.x first-class wire shape.
measured_fields.name: end_line

measured_fields.extraction_rule: The declaration text of the symbol, body and initializer excluded, whitespace collapsed (CODE_SCHEMA section 3). Core-reserved field: it keeps its 1.x first-class wire shape.
measured_fields.name: signature

measured_fields.extraction_rule: Decision points counted in the symbol's body per CODE_SCHEMA section 3.2. Rust (tree-sitter-rust): if expression (including if let; each else if is a nested if) +1; while, for, loop +1 each; match +(arms - 1); the ? operator (try_expression) +1; each && and || in a binary expression +1. TypeScript / JavaScript (tree-sitter-typescript): if +1; for, for-in/for-of, while, do-while +1 each; ternary (?:) +1; switch + (number of case clauses), default not counted; catch +1; each &&, ||, and ?? in a binary expression +1. Python (tree-sitter-python): if +1 and each elif clause +1 (else alone +0); for (including async for) and while +1 each; each except clause +1; conditional expression (x if c else y) +1; each and/or boolean operator +1; inside comprehensions, each for clause +1 and each if clause +1; match + (number of case clauses - 1), case guards not counted separately. Not counted in Python: assert, with, raise, the not operator, comparison chains, else/finally blocks. In every language: a k-way branch contributes k-1 decision points; nested item declarations are never descended into; closures, arrow functions, function expressions, lambdas and comprehensions are not symbols and are descended into. A branch-free function body counts 0. Core-reserved field: it keeps its 1.x first-class wire shape.
measured_fields.name: decisions

siblings.method_text: cyclomatic complexity (McCabe 1976; CODE_SCHEMA §9): v = decision points + 1, decision points counted per CODE_SCHEMA §3.2; only symbols whose decisions were measured are ranked
siblings.name: complexity
siblings.title: Cyclomatic complexity

siblings.method_text: size of a symbol, in lines: end_line - loc.line + 1 (CODE_SCHEMA §9); reported only where end_line was measured
siblings.name: size
siblings.title: Declaration size in lines

siblings.method_text: coupling between objects (Chidamber & Kemerer 1994): the number of distinct types this type is coupled to — a dependency edge (any kind except contains) between this type or one of its methods and another type or one of its methods, in either direction
siblings.name: cbo
siblings.title: Coupling between objects

siblings.method_text: response for a class (Chidamber & Kemerer 1994): the number of this type's methods plus the number of distinct methods of other types they call (external stubs excluded)
siblings.name: rfc
siblings.title: Response for a class

siblings.method_text: lack of cohesion, as raw pair counts (Lanza & Marinescu 2006): over every pair of this type's methods, a pair shares when their recorded accesses overlap — the targets of their reads/writes edges and their recorded references, intersected with the type's member names (its methods plus the targets of its methods' writes); reported as sharing and non-sharing pair counts, never collapsed to a verdict
siblings.name: lcom
siblings.title: Lack of cohesion, as raw pair counts

siblings.method_text: tight class cohesion (Bieman & Kang 1995), over recorded accesses as in lcom: sharing pairs / total method pairs
siblings.name: tcc
siblings.title: Tight class cohesion

siblings.method_text: access to foreign data (Lanza & Marinescu 2006), operationalized: the number of distinct symbols outside this type — variables and methods — targeted by calls, reads, or writes edges from this type's methods (external stubs excluded)
siblings.name: atfd
siblings.title: Access to foreign data

siblings.method_text: weighted methods per class (Chidamber & Kemerer 1994): the sum of the cyclomatic complexities of this type's methods; absent unless every method's complexity was measured
siblings.name: wmc
siblings.oracle: crates/codetopo-core/src/coupling.rs tests (hand-verified type metrics; absence case included)
siblings.title: Weighted methods per class

aggregate_kind.name: package
aggregate_kind.membership_rule: the package of an id is its first segment before the '::' separator (the profile's package rule); boundary-namespace ids belong to no package

siblings.method_text: afferent coupling (Martin 1994): the number of distinct node-to-node dependency pairs (dependency edges per CODE_SCHEMA §9: imports, calls, inherits, implements, defines, reads, writes, references) from other packages into this package
siblings.name: ca
siblings.title: Afferent coupling

aggregate_kind.name: package
aggregate_kind.membership_rule: the package of an id is its first segment before the '::' separator (the profile's package rule); boundary-namespace ids belong to no package

siblings.method_text: efferent coupling (Martin 1994): the number of distinct node-to-node dependency pairs from this package to other packages of the same repository (links to external libraries are not counted here; see external_ce)
siblings.name: ce
siblings.title: Efferent coupling

aggregate_kind.name: package
aggregate_kind.membership_rule: the package of an id is its first segment before the '::' separator (the profile's package rule); boundary-namespace ids belong to no package

siblings.method_text: instability (Martin 1994): Ce / (Ca + Ce); absent when the package has no measured coupling in either direction
siblings.name: instability
siblings.title: Instability

aggregate_kind.name: package
aggregate_kind.membership_rule: the package of an id is its first segment before the '::' separator (the profile's package rule); boundary-namespace ids belong to no package

siblings.method_text: external coupling: the number of distinct node-to-node dependency pairs from this package to external (third-party / stdlib) stub nodes, counted and named separately from ce (CODE_SCHEMA §9, the B0.3 rule) — never merged into it
siblings.name: external_ce
siblings.title: External coupling

title: CODE — CODE_SCHEMA v1.2 as a profile

well_formedness.name: single_definition
well_formedness.rule: A non-boundary symbol is defined in at most one place; violations are first-class diagnostics, not silent merges (CODE_SCHEMA section 5.1).

well_formedness.name: cycles_reported
well_formedness.rule: Cycles over the closure edge set are detected and reported as data; layouts must not hide them (CODE_SCHEMA section 5.2).

well_formedness.name: resolvable_targets
well_formedness.rule: Every edge in the resolvable kinds must resolve to a node or to a boundary stub; unresolved targets are diagnostics, not dropped edges (CODE_SCHEMA section 5.3, generalised by the founding spec to the declared resolvable set).

well_formedness.name: containment_forest
well_formedness.rule: Containment forms a forest: each node has at most one container (CODE_SCHEMA section 5.4).

well_formedness.name: attribute_allow_list
well_formedness.rule: No edge kind may carry attributes outside its declared row (CODE_SCHEMA section 4).

well_formedness.name: provenance_required
well_formedness.rule: An edge whose provenance class requires provenance attributes is refused by the builder when any mandatory attribute is missing (founding spec section 4, R2).
